pairs.en:
## Invocation and praise

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Ever-Merciful.

Praise belongs to God, who has made clear, through the settled stations of aspirational resolve, the ranks and degrees of knowledge by certainty, the eye of certainty and the truth of certainty. Through the stilling of the seekers' anxiety He has clarified their attainment of the utmost that their souls desired, in accordance with their differing degrees in the stations through which they approach knowledge of Him, exalted is He. He has distinguished His elect from the rest of creatures by appointing for them no end other than His very Essence—not any of His worlds, nor any of the presences of His names and attributes. Rather He has made the highest object of their aspirations the noblest objects of His essential knowledge and the highest of His objects of will, so that the ultimate object of their striving is what He wills by Himself for Himself.

From the standpoint of the loftiest aspects of His primary essential affairs (*shuʾūn*) and highest determinations, He Himself is their knowledge of certainty, eye of certainty and truth of certainty throughout the ranks of His essential knowledge. This knowledge is related first to Him and thereafter to what He knows, while they are effaced in Him under the aspect of their own selves, and the ruling of their existence and its diffusion remain throughout His existents and presences.

May God bless the one who has realized this in the most perfect witnessing and in the most complete, exalted and comprehensive knowledge, abiding continually in His presence through all his stations, circumstances, ranks and constitutions—our master Muḥammad, his family, and the elect among his community and brethren who receive from God his most complete legacy of sciences, states and stations. May their special shares, through which they are distinguished from others, bear their fruits along with the effects of following him and the relationships mediated through him. May this blessing continue in its ruling and remain fruitful through the endurance of time, according to time's universal reality and the detailed manifestations of its years, months, days and hours.

## First noble text — Absoluteness is prior to even the attribution of unity

Know that the Real, considered in His essential absoluteness (*iṭlāq dhātī*), cannot rightly be subjected to a judgment, defined through a description or assigned any relation, whether of oneness, necessary existence, principiality, the requirement of bringing into existence, the issue of an effect, or the relation of knowledge directed towards Himself or towards another. All these involve determination and qualification. Every conceivable determination presupposes non-determination; consequently such predicates conflict with sheer absoluteness when applied at that level.

Indeed, even to conceive of the Real's absoluteness it must be conceived as a **negative description**, not as an absoluteness which is merely the opposite of restriction. It is freedom from unity and multiplicity as they are ordinarily conceived; freedom even from limitation to the contrast between absoluteness and qualification, from confinement to their combination, and from confinement to transcendence above either. Consequently affirmation and negation of these predicates, taken at that level, stand alike: neither has precedence over the other. Once this is understood, it becomes clear that the attribution of unity, principiality, influence, the act of making things exist, and the like, is appropriate to the Real **under the consideration of determination**.

The first of the determinations bearing such relations is the intrinsic relation of knowing (*al-nisba al-ʿilmiyya al-dhātiyya*). Its distinction from the Essence is relative, **not a real separation**. By means of this intrinsic relation of knowledge the Real's unity, necessity of existence and principiality may be conceived. In particular, His knowledge of Himself in Himself is the ground of His knowledge of everything. Things are determinations of His universal and detailed intelligitions; quiddities are these intelligitions considered as intelligible forms. Their intelligible ordering is such that some are consequent upon others—not because fresh intelligitions successively arise in God's knowing, which would be unworthy of Him, but because there is an order of ranks within what is eternally and abidingly known. All are eternal intelligitions, remaining in one manner in His knowledge and related to by that knowledge in accordance with what their realities require.

The requirements of those realities can be considered in two ways. The first is their multiplicity being effaced within the unity of the Real: the detailed is understood within the undifferentiated, just as the knowledgeable person may contemplate in a single seed the branches, leaves and fruits that it can produce, and within each fruit a further seed bearing the analogous potential, and so on without end. The second is that the rulings of unity are conceived group after group, each with the quiddities contained within it as forms of the many intelligitions that differentiate the one existence. This is the converse of the first effacement: there multiplicity was absorbed in unity; here unity is, as it were, absorbed in multiplicity. Know this.

Considered in His encompassing absoluteness, the Real bears no name, has no judgment assigned to Him, and is determined by neither description nor mark. Under that standpoint the attribution of exigency or requirement (*iqtiḍāʾ*) has no priority over its denial, for any exigency conceived or rejected would itself be a determinate predicate. Nevertheless, insofar as exigency is considered essential, it has **three ranks**.

In its first rank the determination of its effect depends upon no condition or necessitating factor. In its second rank, it is related to one condition alone. In its third rank, the appearance of its rulings depends upon many conditions, causes and intermediaries. The ruling of the first is essential effusion (*al-fayḍ al-dhātī*), without a necessitating cause and without being conceived as corresponding to a recipient and its receptivity. The second is conditioned by one existential reality: the First Intellect, taken here as the intermediary between the Real and those possible things whose occurrence is apportioned until the Day of Resurrection. The third concerns the plurality of conditions through which effects appear, as in other existents.

I do **not** mean that there are three requirements possessing different realities. It is **one requirement with three ranks**, according to each of which an effect or multiple effects become determinate and manifested. Understand.

## Subsequent divine text — Essential knowledge and the things known

The Real's unitary essential knowledge is described as multiple only insofar as it is related to many objects of knowledge. Apprehension of those objects is realized through the determinations and relations of that knowledge. Its relation to each known thing follows the known thing as it is in itself: whether simple or composite, temporal or spatial, neither temporal nor spatial, receptive at a particular time or without such temporal restriction, finite or unbounded in ruling and description. This must be understood without importing plurality into the reality of the essential knowledge itself.

Among the corollaries is that every judgment made by a judging subject about a judged subject follows both the state of the judge when judging and the state of the judged subject under that judgment. If the subject is of a kind that changes from state to state, the judgments concerning it vary with the states under which it is considered. If it is fixed in one manner, the particular judgment remains fixed according to its definite relation. The judge himself may change through different states, or he may remain stable while the states of the judged object vary. These two considerations exhaust the principal respects under which judgments of any subject and object vary.

Another corollary is that **knowledge follows existence**: wherever existence is found, knowledge is not separated from it. The degrees of knowledge differ according to the degree to which a quiddity receives existence, perfectly or imperfectly. Where existence is received in a more complete manner, knowledge is correspondingly more complete; where receptivity is deficient, knowledge is deficient to the same extent. The predominance of possibility over necessity reverses the proportion previously described. Understand this.

### Completeness of knowing and knowledge of what lies beyond the object

Another corollary of the firmly established texts is this. Although I have briefly indicated aspects of it in some of my other works while discussing other matters, those discussions were expressed in the idiom appropriate to their subject. This book, however, is expressly devoted to the definitive statements derived from the distinctive experiential knowledge of the **station of perfection**, not to the ordinary idioms of restricted unveilings enjoyed by the possessors of particular spiritual stations, whose original grounding lies in the presence of a specific divine name or attribute. I have therefore been obliged to set apart those things that belong to the most comprehensive and perfect station, so that their validity corresponds to what God knows of the thing expressed in the highest, most complete and most perfect degree of His knowledge. I am not concerned merely to establish that a statement is true in relation to one station rather than another, one state or time rather than another, or under some such qualification.

After this universal introduction, I state the text under discussion. Whatever is known by a human being—whether apprehended through consideration, unveiling, sensation or imagination, collectively or individually—has **not** been apprehended perfectly if the knower's consideration, unveiling or other act of apprehension fails to reach what lies **beyond** that thing, even after he has known its essential constituents and universal concomitants. In that case he has attained neither complete apprehension nor genuine comprehensive knowledge of it.

This holds whether the subject is the world in respect of its meanings and spirits, or in respect of its forms and accidents, or the Real Himself. Upon receiving a disclosure of the matter in its clarity, including the mode in which each known reality is determined within divine knowledge, the knower finds the matter as I describe. If knowledge of God has not reached the sheer absoluteness and pure unity of His true Essence—which no name, description, judgment or distinguishing mark identifies, which no witnessing or intellection circumscribes, and which cannot be confined to any specific reality—one has not learned that there is no final aim beyond God, that to encompass Him through knowing or witnessing is impossible, and that beyond unqualified true existence there is only imagined non-being.

There is another way, higher, more complete and more unveiling, to know **why it is impossible to know God as He knows Himself**. By God's favor I have known this by spiritual tasting and witnessing. Its expression and writing down, however, are forbidden; the most that can be said is the indication already given.

A knower may attain the end proper to the divine name whose presence is the orientation of his station. This is especially so under the consideration that the name and the named are identical. Such an end is nevertheless **relative**. Principles and ends mark relative perfections, whereas true perfection transcends them. The Qurʾānic verse “And to your Lord is the ultimate end” (Q 53:42) indicates this. It does not say “your ultimate end is to your Lord” in a manner restricting the end to an individual's attained station. Rather the end of lordship as such is the ultimate end of all ends, beyond which are only endlessly differentiated degrees in greater and greater perfection, without a stopping point.

The Prophet's supplication elucidates this: “I seek refuge in Your good pleasure from Your wrath, in Your pardon from Your punishment, and I seek refuge in You from You. I cannot enumerate praise of You: You are as You have praised Yourself.” In other words, the worshipper cannot compass all that belongs to God. This combines the impossibility of total comprehension with the attainment of the end of all ends in knowledge of the Real. Prophetic reports contain many indications of the same truth for the reader who is alert to them.

The station and taste referred to have several terms of expression. Within Qurʾānic discourse one may refer to the distinguishing signs by which people are known; the ability to discern their marks arises from attaining a culminating standpoint from which one can survey what lies beyond. In the idiom of prophethood it is the *maṭlaʿ*, the rising-point or prospect of the meanings of a verse. A transmitted report refers to the Qurʾān's outward and inward aspects, boundary and rising-point, and to multiple inward depths. I have treated this in my commentary on the Opening (*al-Fātiḥa*). **The variants and chains of that report require separate verification.**

Among the people of God it is called the *mawqif*: the limit of each station, from which the next becomes visible. In the experiential knowledge of the station of perfection, when considered between two stations, it is their encompassing **isthmus** (*barzakh*); in relation to the distinctive station of perfection itself, it is the **isthmus of isthmuses** (*barzakh al-barāzikh*).

### Noble text — Identity, unity, and the first intelligible determination

The unseen of the identity of the Real (*ghayb huwiyyat al-Ḥaqq*) refers to His absoluteness as non-determination. His real unity effaces all considerations, names and attributes. Relations and attributions are expressions of the Real's knowing Himself and apprehending them under the aspect of His determination. Although such determined knowing follows the sheer absoluteness referred to, compared with the determination of the Real in the apprehension of any apprehender under any specific self-disclosure, it is an **unqualified determination**—the most comprehensive determination. It is the witnessing of the perfected ones, the essential self-disclosure, and belongs to the highest station of unification.

The principiality of the Real follows this determination. Principiality is the root of considerations, the source of relations and attributions: those manifest in existence and those concealed within the field of intelligitions and minds. To say of Him that He is one, necessary and unqualified existence concerns the determination of existence within the intrinsic divine relation of knowledge. Under this relation the realized knower calls the Real the Principle (*al-mabdaʾ*), not under an unrelated attribution. Understand and reflect on this: I have included in this text the principle of the principles of divine knowledge. God is the guide.

Every wayfarer, by whichever path he proceeds, has the Real as his ultimate goal, provided he attains some felicity from Him. Thus every such wayfarer has an ascent (*miʿrāj*), and his travelling is an ascension. Understand.

pairs.en:
### Comprehensive noble text — What does it mean for one thing to act upon another?

Know that anything described as possessing causal influence over one thing or several cannot be said to exercise that influence completely unless it affects the very reality of the thing, considered in itself, without adding any other qualification to the essence of the supposed agent, or any external condition whatsoever. I insist on these restrictions because of the effects attributed to things under their specific ranks or under considerations necessarily attached to their realities. I also insist on them because the following opinion has become widespread among speculative thinkers and many people of spiritual tasting: that everything called a mirror, whether intelligible or sensible, has an effect upon the form reflected within it. The rationale is that the mirror reflects the image back to the original, and that the image appears in the mirror in accordance with the mirror's properties.

That assertion is correct **in one respect, but not absolutely**. For the mirror could truly be said to affect the original only if it affected its very reality. It does not. An effect can be ascribed to the mirror in the apprehension of one who does not know the reflected reality itself and has only encountered it in the mirror. The mirror is not a container for the reality of the thing reflected. It is a locus in which its representation and **some** of its appearances are disclosed. The appearance of the form is a relation attributed to the original insofar as its image is impressed in the mirror; it is not itself the reality of the original.

By saying “some of its appearances” I intend an especially important distinction: specific essential self-disclosures (*al-tajalliyāt al-dhātiyya al-ikhtiṣāṣiyya*) do not occur **inside any locus or mirror** or according to any restricted rank. Whoever apprehends the Real through these disclosures witnesses the reality beyond the mirror, as reality itself, not according to a particular manifesting place, name, attribute, state or other determination. He knows by immediate experience that the mirror has no influence upon reality itself.

Our master, the Imam—may God sanctify his spirit—called these the **lightning-like essential disclosures** (*al-tajalliyāt al-dhātiyya al-barqiyya*). At the time I did not know why he called them that or what he meant by the designation. The experience is obtained only by one who has become entirely vacant of the acquired descriptions, states and judgments connected with the necessity of the divine names and with contingent possibility. This is an absolute vacancy, which does not differ from the absoluteness of the Real. Yet it cannot endure for more than a single breath; hence it is likened to lightning.

The reason for its impermanence is the comprehensive nature (*jamʿiyya*) of the human reality. Just as human comprehensiveness does not allow that state to endure, so, if it did not contain the capacity for the vacancy and absoluteness through which this disclosure is received, it would not encompass every description and state. Human comprehensiveness both establishes the possibility of this experience and prevents its permanence. When God granted me this self-disclosure, I found extraordinary effects in my inward and outward being. Though it did not last for two breaths, it left in the locus qualities and sciences whose number none but God could encompass.

On the very night when I wrote down what had come to me, I knew that anyone who had not tasted this witnessing was not fit to bear the inheritance [in the fullest sense]. Nor would such a person grasp the secret of the saying ascribed to the Prophet, “I have with God a time in which none but my Lord can contain me”; nor the saying, “God was and there was nothing with Him”; nor His statement, “Our command is only one, like a flash of the eye” (Q 54:50). Neither could he grasp the secret of principiality in bringing into existence when there was no existing time. **The precise provenance and wording of these transmitted reports are subject to a separate ḥadīth-critical inquiry.**

The one who has tasted this witnessing and who knows that the fixed entities are the realities of existents, that they are not made, that the Reality of the Real is transcendent above being made or being affected, and that there is no third independently existing thing besides the Real and the entities, must realize—provided the vision has been attained in the way I describe—that **nothing produces an effect in the very reality of anything else**. Things are described as affecting their own effects. What people call causes and agents are conditions for the manifestation of the effects of things within their own realities; no separate reality acts upon the intrinsic reality of another.

Understand accordingly the matter of assistance or supply (*madad*). Nothing independently supplies existence to some other thing as though transferring a constituent of itself. Supply reaches the outward from the inward aspect of the thing, and existential luminous disclosure reveals that inward supply. Manifestation is not a modification of the intrinsic reality of what becomes manifest. Relations are described as influencing one another only in the sense that certain relations condition the emergence of others and the appearance of their rulings in the reality from which they arise.

An additional insight of the one tasting this disclosure is that the fixed entities, **insofar as they are mirrors**, have no effect upon the essential divine existential disclosure except the appearance of the multiplicity hidden within that disclosure. Their influence is on the **relation of manifestness**, which is the condition of outward disclosure. The Real is too exalted to be affected by any other, and the realities of beings, inasmuch as they are considered under their own essential realities, are likewise beyond being acted upon by something other than themselves. Under the taste of perfection their realities, in this respect, are the intrinsic affairs of the Real. No mirror, merely as mirror, modifies the reality of what is reflected in it.

Understand and contemplate this text; I have included in it precious sciences and secrets whose value none but God can assess. This is the truth of certainty and the clear definitive text. Anything you hear that conflicts with it, even if correct, is correct only **relatively**; this statement is the unqualified truth without doubt. God is the guide and one who directs.

### Corollaries about causes, fruits, and the uniqueness of every disclosure

Some universal texts have been mentioned in my *Miftāḥ ghayb al-jamʿ wa-tafṣīlihi* and in other writings I composed—not by appropriating other people's words, for God has enriched me with His gifts—but because this book is especially assigned to these texts I must mention the most relevant of them again.

One says: anything that is the cause of multiplicity or many things, **insofar as it is their source**, cannot be determined in some single manifestation or appear to an observer except in relation to the observer's particular field of vision. Another says: a thing does not, from itself as itself, issue forth or produce what contradicts its reality, or what differs altogether from it, whatever the kind of fruit—intelligible, spiritual, imaginal, imaginative, sensible or natural. This is a general principle concerning everything described as a source or a fruitful root, considered simply as itself and under a further subtle consideration apprehended by only a few realized knowers.

When something seems to contradict the principle, the difference arises from **external conditions or qualifications**, and from the configuration produced by the conjunction of the source's reality with those conditions and with the rulings of the rank in which that conjunction becomes determinate. The Qurʾān says: “Each acts according to his own disposition” (Q 17:84).

Nor does a thing produce its very own identical reality, or what is exactly like it in every respect, for that would entail the same existence appearing twice, in one reality, one rank and one manner—an empty re-attainment of what is already attained. Such purposeless repetition would be unworthy of the Real, the wise and knowing Agent. The origin and its fruit must differ in some respect. The contingent possibilities are without end while the effusion of the Real, origin of origins, is one. Thus there is **no repetition in existence** for the one who understands.

For this reason realized masters say that God does not disclose Himself twice to the same person in precisely one form, nor to two different people in precisely the same form. Some respect of distinction must always be present. Remember this; God is the guide.

### Noble text — Gifts of the Essence and gifts of the Names

Know that since no name, attribute or judgment—negative or affirmative—can be attributed to the Real under His absolute aspect, all such predications must concern determinations. Every plurality, whether outwardly existent or intellectually conceived, must be preceded by a unity. Thus the many determinations by which names, attributes and rulings are ascribed to the Real must be preceded by a determination from which all determinations originate. Beyond this first determination is nothing but sheer absoluteness, itself a negative expression that denies to the innermost divine Essence every description, judgment, determination and consideration, as well as confinement to any name or aspect.

One who possesses sound reason, even without authentic unveiling, may reflect on the names and attributes that follow this first determination. If his intellect cannot conceive names and attributes prior to those at which it has arrived, then those are, *relative to his attainment*, names of the Essence. During the veil of discursive reasoning he may infer their precedence from the comprehensiveness of their rulings and the dependency of subsequent names on them. From this principle divine gifts are understood: every benefit that comes from the Real to creatures is either **an essential gift**, **a gift of the names**, or a gift attributable jointly to Essence and names.

Essential gifts do not fall under reckoning; their determinations are not captured or enumerated by number. Gifts of the names, including those jointly attributed to Essence and names, may stand closer to the divine Essence or closer to the domain of names and attributes. Where the relation to names and attributes predominates, the gift is subject to reckoning, easy or difficult according to the strength of the relevant rulings. Where its relation to the Essence predominates, it belongs among gifts without reckoning. A profound secret lies in this matter that cannot be disclosed. What is essential, or possesses a stronger intrinsic relation to the Essence, is given and received through **intrinsic affinity** (*munāsaba dhātiyya*) and not through some other independent necessitating factor.

Without this principle the real meaning of the Qurʾānic descriptions of provision “without reckoning” remains hidden, as in Q 3:27 and Q 24:38, and of the gift “without reckoning” in Q 38:39. A prophetic report likewise speaks of great multitudes of the Prophet's community entering the Garden without reckoning. They receive gifts of the names, but their relation to the Essence is stronger than their relation to names and attributes; hence they follow those who possess intrinsic affinity and share in their states.

Now that we have distinguished the kinds of gifts and their rulings, consider the kinds of recipients. They differ in accordance with the requests constituted by their readiness, spiritual state, station, spirit, natural temperament or accidental natural condition—each of which has, as it were, a language of asking. The highest recipients see the Face of the Real **in the conditions, causes and intermediaries** through which gifts are received. They know by witnessing that these mediating causes are determinations of the Real in divine and cosmic ranks. Between the effusion received and its recipient nothing stands as an independent created efficacy; the effusion is itself differentiated through the particular receptivity in which it becomes manifest. The knower does not suppose that the effusion became fundamentally altered merely by travelling through a chain of intermediary causes and taking on the contingencies of each. He sees the effusion as a manifestation of the inwardness of the Real. Its multiple determinations belong to the rulings of the name *al-Ẓāhir* (the Manifest), for the outward aspect of the Real manifests His inward aspect. Rulings of appearance differentiate the unqualified unity of hiddenness; those rulings are the recipients, the forms of the intrinsic affairs. God speaks the truth and guides whom He wills to a straight path.

### Definitive text — Prayer, right apprehension, and response

A lucid text and universal measure by which divine answering or non-answering, and human compliance, may be known: the complete and valid standard for determining when a servant truly obeys his Lord, and when divine response comes swiftly **in precisely what he asks for**, without substitution or postponement, is **correctness of knowledge** and **perfection of compliance** (*muṭāwaʿa*).

The more accurate one's knowledge and conception of the Real, the swifter the response to the exact matter requested. The more completely one attends to divine commands and hastens to perform them in willing compliance, the greater is the correspondence of divine response to him. For this reason most prayers of the great among the people of God receive an answer, due to the completeness of their compliance and the accuracy of their knowledge and conception of God. The Qurʾān says: “Call upon Me; I will answer you” (Q 40:60).

A person lacking genuine knowledge through witnessing and possessing only a relative, restricted conception is not, in the required sense, directing his prayer to the Real whom God has promised to answer. Rather, he turns to a particular image formed in his mind by his thinking and imagination, or by what he has inherited from the thinking and imagination of others. For this reason response to the *very object* of his request may be withheld or delayed. If such a person nevertheless receives an answer, the explanation can lie in the secret of divine presence with all things, or in the comprehensive concentration characteristic of those in extremity: their necessity gives rise to a readiness for receiving the promised response.

The person who has accurate knowledge and conception, by contrast, brings the Real to presence in his awareness and actually directs his aspiration to Him. His knowledge need not encompass every aspect; even a true orientation through a particular rank, name or attribute suffices to distinguish him from the first case. Such is the condition of the intermediate ranks among the people of God; the former condition is that of the veiled.

The perfected ones and certain unique individuals have a further condition. Their orientation follows the essential self-disclosure through which they have attained the station of perfection. That witnessing yields a comprehensive apprehension of the respects of the divine names, attributes, ranks and considerations. Their conception of the Real is thus sound through the most perfect witnessing, and their prayers are not delayed. Moreover, some of them are admitted to the knowledge of the Preserved Tablet, the rank of the Pen, and even the divine presence of knowing. They recognize what has been allotted to occur; consequently they do not ask for an impossibility which has not been decreed, nor does their aspiration move toward willing it.

I have explicitly mentioned **willing**, because some events are related to the will of such a person without any articulated prayer or request. For many years I witnessed innumerable instances of this in our master—may God sanctify his spirit. He told me that in one of his spiritual occurrences he had seen the Prophet, who gave him the glad tidings: “God is quicker to respond to you than you are to turn to Him in supplication.”

This is a station above that of prayers being answered, and derives from perfected compliance; indeed it lies above the station normally termed compliance. The latter means hastening to obey commands, seeking the things pleasing to God, and fulfilling divine rights as far as one is able. Qūnawī here adduces reports concerning the Prophet and Abū Ṭālib to illustrate divine responsiveness. **Their precise wording and historical attribution require examination; they are preserved here as reports cited in the primary text, not certified historical evidence.**

The higher station returns to the servant's essential reality corresponding completely to what the Real wills for him by the first universal will. That will relates to the complete bringing to light and self-manifestation (*al-jalāʾ wa-l-istijlāʾ*) for which the cosmos is created. The **perfect human** (*al-insān al-kāmil*) is specifically the intended locus; everything else is intended in a derivative manner, insofar as what is necessary for realizing an end is also willed for the sake of that end.

The perfect human is intended as such because he is the complete mirror of the Real. Through him the Real is manifested with respect to His Essence and all His names, attributes, rulings and considerations, in the manner in which He knows Himself and the realities of His objects of knowledge. The mirror must not impose a deficiency of receptivity or distortion such that what is displayed differs from what it is in itself. One whose reality is so constituted has no will standing apart from the will of the Real. He is the mirror of his Lord's will and the other attributes. Accordingly his supplication is effaced into a will not opposed to divine will, and what he wills occurs in accordance with the divine saying “Doer of whatever He wills” (Q 85:16).

If he supplicates, he does so as a mirror of all the worlds, speaking in their tongues and ranks. If he refrains from supplication, he does so under his aspect as a locus of manifestation turned toward the divine presence. Beyond this station is no further station to which a traveller could aspire. Beneath it stands the person whose sound conception and perfected knowledge make him a genuine addressee of “Call upon Me; I will answer you”; the promised divine response is true. Other forms of address and orientation cannot be treated as possessing precisely the same conditions.

Understand this and you will attain precious secrets and extraordinary sciences that discursive thinking and written exposition have not reached. God is the guide.

### Noble text — Knowing through union and the one knowledge of the many

Know that the highest degree of knowledge of a thing, whoever knows it and whether the thing known is single or manifold, is realized through union with the known and the absence of otherness between knower and known. For the reason that ignorance prevents complete apprehension is the predominance of the factor by which the two are distinct. Distinction constitutes an intelligible distance, and distance prevents perfected apprehension. The ranks of knowledge vary with the predominance of that through which the knower and the known are one; this is true nearness, overcoming the separation that is true distance.

If you witness and taste this through a verified unveiling, you will know that the perfection of the Real's knowledge of things comes from His manifesting them to Himself within Himself, their plurality and otherness being absorbed within His unity. For a thing's being present in any locus, intelligible or formal, is in accordance with the way it is determined and displayed there. Hence we say that the Real knows Himself through Himself and knows things in Himself through the very knowledge through which He knows Himself. The report that God was when nothing was with Him points to the absence of the things' otherness when considered in the unity in which they are contained; their later differentiated consideration does not invalidate the priority of the Real in unity.

When the multiplicity of things that had previously been implicit in unity becomes individually intelligible, and the judgment of unity is brought together with their distinction, the perfection previously hidden in unity becomes outwardly disclosed. Thus there opens the door of perfected manifestation and self-manifestation (*jalāʾ* and *istijlāʾ*), which is the genuine object of the process. The judgments of unity appear within multiplicity and those of multiplicity within unity.

Unity makes multiplicity one by becoming the common existential respect among many things distinguished in their intrinsic realities; by gathering these things in itself, it connects what distinguishes them. The many, in turn, cause the One to appear as many through determinations that diversify its appearance, like colouring and the qualities required by the differing preparedness of the numerous loci of one self-disclosure. Thus comes the differentiation of knowledge of kinds of disclosure and their accompanying rulings, including the relational effects of making and undoing, outwardly and inwardly, above and below, within time and beyond particular time, in correspondence or lack of correspondence. All this rests on the connecting disclosure of the One that gathers the manifold.

Knowledge, delight and felicity vary with *munāsaba*, the proportion of affinity; ignorance, suffering and misery vary with the strength of separation and difference. Where the rulings of joining and separation intermingle, the relative dominance of each determines the outcome. The common source and reference-point of a cluster of such rulings in a particular kind of affinity is a **rank** (*martaba*). Understand.

As I began writing this text, it was said to me inwardly that the rulings belonging to unity and to the one Real—referred to as the rulings of necessity—derive, from the standpoint of unity, from **one ruling**, the reality of *qaḍāʾ* (decree). The apportioned measures (*maqādīr*) arise through the plurality of known things under that one ruling. The appearing of one existence according to that plurality has a primary effect, and then a secondary effect in the measured things by returning their influence to them. Reflect on this unusual distinction; God is the guide.

### Further noble text — Two signs of complete knowledge of something other than the Real

The highest degree of knowledge of any thing **other than the Real** is to know it by a knowledge resulting from seeing it completely within divine knowledge. There are two signs of this attainment. First, the knowledge obtained is sufficient, so that one has no need to revisit and reconsider the subject in pursuit of increased knowledge. An increase after one has claimed already to know it demonstrates that the earlier knowledge was incomplete. Complete knowledge of an object would leave nothing additional to discover about it, as is the case of divine knowledge, and requires complete intellectual encompassment of the known.

The second sign is that the ruling of knowledge extends beyond the object's restricted determination until one apprehends its ultimate limit as joined to the absoluteness of the Real. Knowledge of the Real Himself, however, is not like this. What is known of Him is only what appears through some determination in a rank, locus, state, respect or consideration. Whenever a particular determination comes within one's grasp, a further determination of the unqualified Essence becomes manifest to the knower according to the state under which the Real is now disclosed. Human states do not reach a final point at which they cease to change, and the modes of the Real's manifestation to human beings likewise do not come to an end.

I have previously indicated that the names are names of states. The fixed entities are subject to the passing of states over them, whereas the Real is disclosed in the states, as indicated by “Every day He is upon some affair” (Q 55:29). Understand. Do not be satisfied merely with reinterpretation: strive to witness first, then trust and surrender; God grants success.

### Noble text — Every absolute thing has a conditional respect

No existent in the world described as unqualified lacks a respect in which it is conditioned—even if only by the way it is determined within the conception of one or more knowers. Likewise no existent judged conditioned lacks some respect in which it relates to absoluteness. Only one who knows things perfectly after knowing the Real, and knows the respects by which they are understood, can apprehend this. Whoever has not tasted this witnessing has not yet fully realized knowledge of the Real and the created order.

### Text — Essential perfection and the appearance of greater perfection

The Real has an essential perfection and a perfection of the names whose outward manifestation is related to the creation of the cosmos. Under the consideration of **determination**, both may be called perfections of the names: every judgment about an object presupposes that the object has been distinguished within the judge's knowledge. Were the Essence not first conceived as distinct by its intrinsic independence from all else, one would not describe a perfection as “essential.” Every determinate respect considered of the Real may be called a name, for the names, according to the realized knowers, are determinations of the Real.

Under this respect all perfection ascribed to Him may be called a perfection of the names. But from another respect, the generation of the names from the presence of His unity belongs to the requirements of His own reality; accordingly every perfection ascribed to Him may be called **essential**. From this distinction it follows that an intrinsic perfection does not become deficient when external accidents or concomitants appear in some ranks; nor can an inherent defect be imagined that these accidents would repair. Rather, in certain ranks the description of **greater perfection** (*akmaliyya*) comes into appearance, including the realization that the intrinsic perfection is unaffected by those manifestations.

### Very noble text — The reality of the Real and that of the creature

The reality of the Real is the form of His knowledge of Himself considered under the determination of His knowing Himself, where knower, knowledge and known are one. His intrinsic attribute, not distinct from His Essence, is the oneness of a comprehensive gathering (*aḥadiyyat jamʿ*) beyond which no further gathering, relation or consideration is conceivable. To witness and know this attribute properly is to recognize that the Real is called determined within each determined thing in accordance with the respect that permits His apprehension there, **without** thereby being restricted to that determination. He is in Himself not determined even while one predicates determination of Him under the aspect of manifestation, whether one considers the locus identical with what appears or distinct from it.

The reality of the created order is the form of its Lord's knowledge of it. Its intrinsic attribute is **poverty** (*faqr*) of the kind that opens upon unqualified sufficiency—not every poverty indiscriminately. Understand.

### Very noble text — Three modes of transcendence (*tanzīh*)

The result of **rational transcendence** (*tanzīh ʿaqlī*) is to distinguish the Real from what is called “other” through negative attributes, in order to ward off defects imagined by the intellect though not existing as independent realities. The outcome of **revealed or scriptural transcendence** (*tanzīh sharʿī*) is to deny multiple independent existences and partnership in the rank of divinity. Scripture maintains this even when created things share the linguistic predication of affirmative qualities with God, so as to exclude equality and likeness. Hence verses speak of God as the best of providers, best of forgivers, most excellent of creators and most merciful of the merciful, and say that God is greater.

**Transcendence according to unveiling** (*tanzīh kashfī*) affirms comprehensive gathering in the Real without circumscription, while distinguishing the distinct rulings of the names. Not every effect can properly be attributed to every divine name: some relations are impossible for certain names though true of others. The same holds for the attributes. Its fruit is the denial of independent otherness without denying that numerical distinctions appear under their own respect, without presuming either an external defect to negate or an acquired perfection to append. Peace.

### Noble text — The locus conditions how something is present

The presence or being of anything within anything else follows the nature of the locus, whether that locus is intelligible or formal. Thus possible things, considered as eternally determined and represented in divine knowledge, are described in respect of their fixed intelligible relations as eternal; considered under another aspect, however, each determination also bears a relation to origination. The world's existence and the knowledge of its inhabitants are originated and receptive; divine existence and knowledge are not. Know this and you will be guided, God willing.

### Comprehensive noble text — Divine names and the ranks of their determination

The word **Essence** (*dhāt*) is appropriately applied to the Real only under a determination: the first intelligible determination following, in the understanding of those not perfected, the nameless, indescribable absoluteness which is indicated only negatively. The positive determination is first; it encompasses intrinsically the essential names, **keys of the unseen** (*mafātīḥ al-ghayb*), and the Essence named is not distinct from these names in any respect. The names differ among themselves and may stand in opposition, though they are also united under the all-inclusive Essence. Unity of singularity (*aḥadiyya*) describes determination, not the absolutely unqualified as such: the latter bears neither name nor attribute.

From the aspect that these names are not other than the Essence, one can say that the Real acts essentially. There is one intrinsic concomitant of the Essence, distinguished from it **only relatively**: **knowledge** (*ʿilm*). Unity is affirmed of the Real under the consideration of knowledge, for in and through it the rank of divinity, the other ranks, and all objects of knowledge become determined and inscribed. Knowledge is a mirror of the Essence with its essential names, which are not other than the Essence itself. It is the root and source of intelligible multiplicity. To call it a mirror of the known realities and of the Essence is to consider its distinction from Essence as a conceptual one through which the Real's knowing of Himself in Himself can be expressed. His essential knowledge is, as it were, a mirror of Himself.

As we have said elsewhere, the reality of the Real is the form of His knowledge of Himself. Every thing made manifest in a locus is distinct from that locus in some respect, **except that the Real may be said to be both the appearing and the locus under the different considerations explained**. Do not turn this into a multiplication of independent existents.

Ranks are comprehensive determinations contained in the single intrinsic concomitant—knowledge. They resemble stations through which the unqualified effusion passes, in the sense already explained concerning the relation of disclosure to what is disclosed. They have a qualified role in the manifestation of causal effects, not independent causality. Every rank is an intelligible locus in which a grouping of the rulings of necessity and possibility appears, from the essential names and the principal divine names and their derivative names. Ranks have fixed entities within the field of knowledge and intelligition. Their influence is not independent: it occurs through existence. By the way the effusion is determined in their receptivity, the ranks function like forms or moulds that condition the appearance of what passes through them. They are thus points of gathering, sources and returns of relational effects. Understand.

The ranks are understood as proceeding from one another, and similarly the names. Divinity (*ulūhiyya*) with its chief names—Living, Knowing, Willing and Powerful—is the shadow of the Essence considered as containing the keys of the unseen. A subtle distinction remains: divinity can be considered as distinct from the principal names, whereas the Essence cannot be distinguished from its **essential** names by the one who witnesses essential disclosure. Any such distinction is a product of the understanding of someone veiled from that disclosure. The names differ in their relations while remaining inseparable; some follow others, as Creator, Originator and Fashioner follow their own principal names. Remember this.

### Connection concerning the secret of affinities

The secret of affinities (*munāsabāt*) is participation in a respect that removes the rulings of mutual otherness from precisely the aspect in which affinity is established. Their first and highest form is **intrinsic affinity** (*munāsaba dhātiyya*). Such affinity between the Real and the human being who is specifically intended is established under two aspects.

First, the human being's mirrorhood exerts only a weak modifying effect upon the self-disclosure determined in him. That is, the mirror does not give the disclosed Real any character that compromises His holiness; there is only the qualification of determination, which cannot impair the divine greatness, majesty or unity. Such a person is free of most of the limitations of possibility and of the properties of the intermediaries. From this perspective the degrees of the intimate ones and the unique individuals differ.

The second aspect of affinity with the Real is the servant's share of **the form of the divine presence**. This share varies according to his comprehensiveness (*jamʿiyya*). Affinity grows stronger or weaker as the circle of his comprehensive capacity widens or narrows; sometimes he receives a fuller portion, and at other times less.

The one who encompasses the attributes and rulings of the ranks of necessity and possibility, and everything of them that can become actual in each age and time, while also possessing the first kind of affinity, has **perfection**. He is loved by the Real and intended for his own sake. By the reality of being the **isthmus of isthmuses** (*barzakh al-barāzikh*), he is the mirror both of the Essence and of divinity with their concomitants. One who possesses only the first aspect of intrinsic affinity may be beloved and brought near, but is not thereby the all-comprehensive perfect human. I have indicated this distinction earlier.

### Intrinsic affinity between people: temperament and spirituality

Intrinsic affinity among human beings likewise arises under two aspects, parallel to the two just mentioned. One is a shared **temperament** (*mizāj*): the degrees of temperamental equilibrium occupied by the two persons may coincide within the range of human temperaments, or one degree may stand next to the other. This is a major principle in the way of realization, though few truly know it by taste.

The differentiation of human spirits and their ranks of nobility and elevation is connected to the number and distance of intermediaries, and to how the rulings of possibility increase or decrease with them. After the prior decree and determination of God, bodily temperament is the condition according to which a particular spirit is determined. What approaches the point of true equilibrium—the center proper to the perfected souls—is capable of receiving a more noble spirit with a higher relationship to the ranks of superior intellects and souls. What stands farther from that point has a correspondingly lower relation. The preceding statement about shared temperaments is therefore a preliminary to knowing the **spiritual affinity** of the second aspect, which resembles the hidden and pure intrinsic affinity with the Real.

When you understand this through witnessed disclosure or verified understanding, you will see that some spirits have their origin of determination in the Preserved Tablet, others in the spirituality of the Throne under the station associated with Isrāfīl, others in the Footstool under Mīkāʾīl, and others in the Lote Tree under Jibrīl. The ranks descend to the nearest heaven, whose governing angel Qūnawī here calls Ismāʿīl. The variation in their degrees depends, after the precedence of divine knowledge, providence, decree and will, upon temperaments and their nearness to or distance from equilibrium. Divine care and will appear in the proper formation of the body, followed by the breathing of the spirit and its determination.

**Editorial caution:** these are medieval metaphysical, angelological and physiological correspondences. Their hierarchy and reported names should be documented as source claims, not silently presented as scientific facts or universally accepted theological assertions.

### Rank-based affinities and the origins of spirits

Affinities based on rank (*munāsaba martabiyya*) have several forms. One concerns the original mines or sources of determination of spirits. The highest human spirits—the spirits of the perfected—have their principial rank in the Mother of the Book (*Umm al-Kitāb*). Others are determined through the Supreme Pen, also termed the First Intellect and Universal Spirit; others through the Preserved Tablet; others through the throne-related rank of Isrāfīl, the Footstool and Mīkāʾīl, the Lote Tree and Jibrīl, and then the other classes descending to the ruler of the nearest heaven. Qūnawī reports the correspondence of the last with the **Active Intellect** of the Peripatetic philosophers.

Another form of rank-based affinity depends on **imaginal manifestations**. Spirits at their diverse ranks have forms or loci in which they become manifest. Apart from the perfected, the first such human locus is the **absolute imaginal world** (*ʿālam al-mithāl al-muṭlaq*). Even where an imaginative form has its materials in the subtle powers of the natural constitution, and in purified spiritual capacities, its manifestations in the Garden depend upon the spirituality, powers and properties of those original imaginal forms.

The dwellings of the inhabitants of Paradise are thus signs of the ranks of their spirits in relation to the Real and their primary imaginal manifestations. Qūnawī cites reports concerning the proximity of dwellings in the Garden and the ability of believers to recognize their own dwellings there. He interprets these reports through affinity and rank rather than crude spatial distance alone.

The **market of Paradise**, containing beautiful human forms that inhabitants may choose to assume, is described as part of the river-system or channels of the absolute imaginal world. It is a source of imaginal forms and of supplies communicated to the spirits of the inhabitants. Their food, drink, clothing and other joys are manifested according to the planes of their deeds, convictions, traits, states and degrees of equilibrium. Qūnawī thereby ties eschatological imagery to his account of imaginal receptivity rather than treating it as merely an analogue of material goods.

The robes of honor and gifts carried by angels to the generality of the people of Paradise when they are brought to the hill of vision for an audience with the Real manifest the rulings of names and attributes upon which these visitors depend, even when they do not know it. The gifts strengthen their affinity with the Real, renewing the subtle threads connecting them with Him through the names and attributes having lordly authority over them.

The command to the angels, “Return them to their palaces,” is interpreted as the ending of the particular rulings through which they had been gathered in the audience. When the opposed rulings of names that distinguish and separate come into effect, the visitors again experience separation and veil. The diversity of their ranks during the audience follows their standing before the Real, the accuracy of their beliefs, their knowledge and genuine witnessings, and the degree to which they preferred the divine presence above other things in their earlier lives. The length of their company, the honor of the address made to them and what they apprehend of it all vary accordingly. Their apprehension is also conditioned by how they present to themselves what they knew or believed of God, and by the particular disclosure associated with the hill of vision.

### The perfected ones and modes of posthumous affinity

The condition of the **perfected** is different. They have passed beyond the presences of names and attributes and the self-disclosures particular to them, reaching the field of **essential disclosure**. Qūnawī adduces a report describing a class of inhabitants of Paradise from whom the Lord does not conceal Himself. Because they cannot be confined by Paradise, another world, time, place or any particular presence, they are with Him wherever He is, in a manner that is not defined by *where*, bodily distance, a veil, a journey to an audience, or a meeting whose duration ends under a temporal ruling. Thus their state does not depend on periodic transit through specific places of visitation. Seek a portion of their high ranks, for God is the bestower of good.

As for affinities between people through their **intermediate or barzakh** ranks, the Prophet's account of the Night Journey provides an example. He saw Adam in the nearest heaven with multitudes of his descendants to his right and left, the blessed and the wretched, and Adam's different response to the two. Qūnawī reads this as an indication of ranks corresponding to general felicity and misery after death. The wretched differ in their degrees; he records reports concerning locations where certain spirits are gathered. In the highest regions of the nearer world the blessed also differ, and more particular stations are associated in the Night Journey with prophets in the succeeding heavens—Jesus, Joseph, Idrīs, Aaron, Moses and Abraham, peace upon them.

Those participating in the prophetic legacies inherit differentiated ranks under these spiritual stations. But the visions of those seven prophets need not exhaust the ranks of all messengers, prophets, saints and inheritors: many others have their own degrees. Qūnawī adduces a report of multiple ascensions of the Prophet and appeals to Abū Nuʿaym in connection with their transmission. **The exact number, provenance and authenticity of that report remain to be verified.**

The sevenfold mapping is, on his argument, an **example** of particular correspondences operative in one disclosure, not a final exhaustive inventory of prophetic ranks. Thus one prophet can be associated with another in certain manifestations—for example John (Yaḥyā) may be understood as sharing a station now with Jesus and now with Aaron—because of an affinity of attributes, activities or states. Think about this and you may be guided, God willing.

pairs.en:
### Very noble text — Existence is one without being the opposite of multiplicity

Know that the Real is **pure existence** (*al-wujūd al-maḥḍ*), in which there is no difference, and that He is one by a genuine unity. This unity is not conceived as the opposite of multiplicity, nor does its reality or the correct conception of it depend on conceiving an opposite. Rather it is established through itself, establishing and not requiring to be established. When we say “unity,” we do so to indicate transcendence and to facilitate understanding, **not** to ascribe to the Real the restricted notion of unity conceived in veiled minds.

Considered in this unity, in abstraction from loci of manifestation and from attributes assigned according to manifestation and His appearing in them, He cannot be apprehended, encompassed, known, named or described. Whatever a person perceives within concrete entities or witnesses in the cosmos, by whatever mode or in whichever presence, insofar as it is perceived *in a locus*, is of a different order. The exception is knowledge of intelligible realities as they are in the unseen rank, apprehended by unveiling. What is apprehended in a locus comprises colours, lights, surfaces and the manifold differences of quality and quantity. Their analogues appear in the imaginal world connected with the human constitution, or within the imaginal world considered in another respect as separate from it. Their plurality is sensible; any unity affirmed of them is intellectually apprehended or intuited.

All these are rulings of existence, forms of the relations of divine knowledge, or attributes accompanying existence under the consideration of its relation to the entities in which it appears and through which it is made manifest. However one describes these appearances, **they are not existence itself**. Existence is one and is not grasped through anything considered as other than it. The one insofar as it is one is not apprehended through plurality simply insofar as it is plural, and conversely. A human being does not apprehend something through a unity completely identical to the unity of existence: apprehension requires his existence, life, possession of knowledge, and an affinity between him and the thing approached, together with the removal of obstacles. He therefore apprehends through the many respects of his constitution, not through the sheer oneness devoid of all multiplicity. I have explained further secrets of this point in *Kashf sirr al-ghayra ʿan sirr al-ḥayra*, and more will follow elsewhere.

### Existence and quiddities: the fixed entities are known, not independently made

Existence in respect of the Real is identical with His Essence. In respect of any other existent, existence is conceptually added to its reality. The reality of each existent is the relation of its eternal determination within its Lord's knowledge: the realized knowers call this its **fixed entity** (*ʿayn thābita*); other thinkers call it a quiddity, a known non-existent, a fixed thing, or something similar.

From the standpoint of the unity of His existence, nothing proceeds from the Real but **one**, for what is simply one as one cannot bring forth a plurality under precisely that same respect. Yet what proceeds as one is not, in our account, a separately existing First Intellect in the manner described by certain philosophers. It is the **general existence effused** upon the entities of generated beings, including those that have become outwardly actual and those whose actuality is eternally known but not yet manifested. This one existence is shared by the Supreme Pen, also named the First Intellect and described as the first existent, and by all the other existents. According to realized knowledge there is not a third independent ontological class between the Real and the world. The world consists of realities known by the Real under their determinations and described by their relation to existence.

Because the determinate images of these realities are eternally known in the intrinsic divine knowledge, those realities **under that respect** cannot themselves be things newly made. To make them in the essential knowing would require originated changes in God and would construe the divine Essence as either a container for other things or something contained. They are not called produced or made because what is produced through creation is the *existence* manifested under their determinations. A thing without independent existence cannot become an independently produced existent merely by being eternally known.

If it were said that their intrinsic determinations were made, either they would have to possess the same existential rank as the divine Knower, or the Knower would have to be a subject acted upon by His own action within Himself. Both alternatives violate the unqualified unity and independence being affirmed. Nor can the effused existence be conceived as simply an accident received by a separately existent possible substance already possessing the existence to receive it. That would involve duplicating what one had already presupposed. The entities, under the consideration mentioned, are thus **unmade**; and there are not two existences in rivalry but one existence shared across the possible things and derived from the Real.

This one existence related to contingent things does not differ in **existential reality** from the unmanifest existence of the Real abstracted from determinate loci, except through relations and considerations: manifestness, determination, plurality through association with loci, the ruling of common predication, and other descriptions that arise through connection with manifestations. The source of these manifestations in relation to His self-disclosure is the rank of the *ʿamāʾ*, mentioned in a prophetic report, the station of divine descent and an outpouring of generosity from the unseen of identity. The first unseen and eternal relation of mutual orientation is posited in this rank, by which the presences of divine names open through essential eternal orientations. The details of this imagery must be considered carefully; the term *ʿamāʾ* and the report underlying it require textual and ḥadīth verification.

### Two considerations of existence; essential knowledge neither increases nor changes

Existence has two considerations. First, inasmuch as it is sheer existence, it is the Real. Under this respect there is neither multiplicity nor composition, neither attribute, name, description, relation nor judgment, but pure existence. Even our naming it “existence” is only a concession to understanding, not an adequate true name. Name, attribute and Essence are not three distinct entities here. Its perfection is intrinsic existence arising from itself and not another. His life and power are identical in reality with His knowledge. His eternal knowledge of things is the same as His knowledge of Himself: He knows Himself through Himself and everything through the knowledge by which He knows Himself.

In Him differing things are gathered without containing or being contained as physical vessels; multiplicities proceed through the appearances permitted by His singularity. His unity is the origin of every multiplicity, His simplicity is the ground upon which all composition may be understood, and His priority and finality, manifestness and hiddenness, are not two opposed changes of state within the Essence. No conceptual opposition between unity and multiplicity, or between absoluteness and restriction, can capture the whole truth. The Real's comprehensive meaning pervades every articulated relation, and His perfection embraces every genuine quality. Even what appears deficient to the veiled knower can, under the appropriate disclosure, be seen as an expression of some divine perfection, a locus for majesty or beauty. The many names and attributes do not destroy the unity of what they name, nor does the Real need external manifestation in order to perfect Himself.

His veil, majesty, independence and holiness mean that His reality is other than what would oppose it, and that nothing outside it establishes or preserves His existence. No thing is established by itself or through another except in dependence on Him. Intellects and reflections cannot comprehend Him under that respect, nor can spatial directions contain Him, nor inward or outward witnessing encompass Him. He is above bodily and intelligible restrictions, quantitative or qualitative estimation, and the total knowledge of created faculties, perfected or imperfect. Rational negations describe what He is **not**, and yet cannot confer comprehensive true acquaintance with His holiness.

The ground of His knowledge of the cosmos is His knowledge of Himself; the appearance of its relations is the appearance of the known realities. He knows indefinitely many things both because His knowledge embraces all that is known and because He is their source. He knows His Essence and its concomitants and the concomitants of those concomitants collectively and severally, generally and distinctly, without limit. What is determined according to a condition or cause He eternally knows **with its condition, cause and consequence**; what is not so determined He knows through Himself in the way He wills. His knowledge does not become new, and no created judgment restricts Him to a particular changing state.

His perfection belongs to Himself, His existence is actual rather than potential and necessary rather than possible. He is above change and origination. Created things do not contain Him, whether to reveal or shelter Him, and He does not create them to repair His own need. Things are related to Him as their source of determination; He is not related to their independence in the manner they are related to His necessity. They depend upon Him for their existence, but He does not depend upon them.

### Providence and determined manifestation

The relation of things to the Real is called **providential care** (*ʿināya*). Their veil from Him consists in ignorance, deception and imagination, paradoxically arising because of the extremity of His nearness and His exalted majesty. Providence, in its true sense, is the effusion of His existential light upon the form inscribed in the mirror of each fixed entity—an entity considered as a relation of being known—and made ready to receive His ruling of bringing it into outward existence and manifesting Himself through it. “There is nothing like Him” (Q 42:11) pertains to the first consideration; “He is the Hearing, the Seeing” pertains to the second.

Whenever He is apprehended, witnessed, addresses another or is addressed, His unqualified self remains behind the veil of His majesty. The event involves the relation of manifestness, the self-disclosure of nearness, and the shining of universal existential light upon possible realities. It is not the joining of two independent substances. In this conditioned aspect the determination of existence under the properties of possible entities, their affairs, special properties, accidents, periods, ranks and locations is called **creation** and “otherness.” Under that aspect every name and description can be predicated of it through its manifestations, and the appropriate faculties apprehend the various forms.

The light pervading these loci is nonetheless holy above division, spatial partition or **indwelling** (*ḥulūl*) in spirits and bodies. It becomes manifest when and as He wills. It is capable of being considered under the two opposed rulings of unqualified freedom from forms and conditioned manifestation through them, not because an external constituent is added to the Real but because of different relations. When He wills a form appears; without such willing no form is attributed under the aspect of that particular creation. Apparent individualization through forms does not lessen His majesty, perfection or holiness. Like an image shown in a changing mirror, the determination alters within the locus, not within the underlying unqualified reality.

Through existential disclosure, hidden things become visible and blessings pass from the unseen to the witnessed world under the names **Expander** (*al-Bāsiṭ*) and **Originator** (*al-Mubdiʾ*). When the ruling of intimate nearness is lifted, those outwardly manifest become hidden under the names **Contracter** (*al-Qābiḍ*) and **Restorer** (*al-Muʿīd*). Under the standpoint of concealment by majesty He is Forgiving or Concealing (*Ghafūr*); when He loves to be known and appears as He wills, He is Loving (*Wadūd*). Through love He brings the realities forth and draws them back. Nothing escapes His grasp, irresistible power or volition.

Qūnawī identifies the glorious Throne, in this technical context, as a locus of the display of power, wisdom and the ordered effects of unveiling and concealment. He connects the sequence of divine names with Q 50:37 and Q 85:12–16, culminating in “Doer of whatever He wills.” The final phrase blocks the error of treating the ranked order or its first intermediary as necessary to divine efficacy: the Real acts according to His will, not because He is constrained by an independent cause.

### Last noble text — No independent appearance of the fixed entities

Know that the greatest doubts and veils arise when the multiplicities taking place **within the one existence** are mistaken for the fixed entities themselves having become existent. These multiplicities arise together with the **effects** of the fixed entities, but the entities, considered in themselves, have never appeared and will never appear. In themselves they do not require their own outward manifestation.

If a realized knower speaks otherwise, or ascribes existence and manifestness to the entities, his speech follows the language of a particular rank or a restricted spiritual taste. It can be true in relation to a particular station or group of stations, without being the truth proper to the all-comprehensive station of perfection. What I have explained is the **definitive statement that cannot be superseded** by a higher station. In this book I have stated matters from that standpoint. Other utterances may be equally true unconditionally or may be true only in relation to their specific stations.

Understand, therefore, that manifestation belongs to **existence**, but under the condition of multiplicity with the effects of the entities in it. Hiddenness belongs intrinsically to the fixed entities and also to existence considered in the unity that cannot be partitioned. Matters move between appearance and concealment according to the strength and predominance of their rulings. What diminishes under the aspect of the manifest is included under the aspect of the hidden, and conversely. Relations and attributions are forms of states and rulings that arise among ranks: some manifest others and some conceal others according to the relative predominance already mentioned. Understand.

**End of the independently printed original text.** Praise belongs to God alone; may God bless our master Muḥammad, his family and companions and grant them peace.

pairs.ar: نصّ شريف هو أول النصوص الواجب تقديمه: اعلم أن الحق من حيث إطلاقه الذاتي لا يصح أن يحكم عليه بحكم، أو يعرّف بوصف، أو يضاف إليه نسبة ما من وحدة، أو وجوب وجود، أو مبدئية، أو اقتضاء إيجاد، أو صدور أثر، أو تعلق علم منه بنفسه أو غيره؛ لأن كل ذلك يقضي بالتعين والتقيد، ولا ريب في أن تعقل كل تعين يقضي بسبق اللاتعين، فكل ما ذكرناه ينافي الإطلاق، بل تصور إطلاق الحق يشترط فيه أن يتعقل بمعنى أنه وصف سلبيّ، لا بمعنى أنه إطلاق ضد التقييد، بل هو إطلاق عن الوحدة والكثرة المعلومتين، وعن الحصر أيضا في الإطلاق والتقييد، وفي الجمع بين كل ذلك والتنزه عنه، فيصح في حقه كل ذلك حال تنزّهه عن الجميع، فنسبة كل ذلك إليه وغيره وسلبه عنه على السواء، ليس أحد الأمرين بأولى من الآخر، وإذا وضح هذا علم أن نسبة الوحدة إلى الحق والمبدئية والتأثير والفعل الإيجادي ونحو ذلك إنما يصح وينضاف إلى الحق باعتبار التعين.
pairs.en: A noble text, the first of the texts that must be placed at the beginning. Know that, with respect to His essential nondelimitation, the Real cannot be subjected to a judgement, defined by an attribute, or assigned any relation whatsoever: whether unity, necessity of existence, principiality, the requirement of bringing something into existence, the issuing of an effect, or the relation of His knowledge to Himself or another. Each of these entails determination and restriction; indeed, conceiving any determination presupposes nondetermination. Everything just named therefore conflicts with the intended sense of absoluteness. To conceive the Real’s absoluteness one must understand it negatively, not as an absoluteness opposed to restriction. It is free of the familiar unity and multiplicity, free even of being confined to absoluteness, restriction, their conjunction, or transcendence of both. The Real is not enclosed by any of these alternatives: in this consideration neither predication nor its denial takes precedence. It follows that unity, principiality, causal efficacy, and the act of bringing into being are rightly attributed to the Real only under a consideration of determination.

pairs.ar: وأول التعينات المتعلقة: النسبة العلمية الذاتية، لكن باعتبار تميزها عن الذات بالامتياز النسبي لا الحقيقي، وبواسطة النسبة العلمية الذاتية يتعقل وحدة الحق ووجوب وجوده ومبدئيته، وسيما من حيث أن علمه بنفسه في نفسه في نفسه، وأن عين علمه بنفسه سبب لعلمه بكل شيء، وأن الأشياء عبارة عن تعيّنات تعقلاته الكلية والتفصيلية، وأن الماهيات عبارة عن التعقلات، وأنها تعقلات منتشئة التعقل بعضها من بعض، لا بمعنى أنها تحدث في تعقل الحق تعالى، تعالى اللّه عما لا يليق به. بل تعقل البعض من متأخر الرتبة عن البعض، وكلها تعقلات أزلية أبدية على وتيرة واحدة، تتعقل في العلم ويتعلق بها بحسب ما تقتضيه حقائقها.
pairs.en: The first of the relevant determinations is the essential relation of knowledge. Its distinction from the Essence is relational, not real. Through this essential relation of knowledge, the Real's unity, necessary existence, and principiality become intelligible, especially insofar as His knowledge of Himself is itself the ground of His knowledge of everything. Things are the determinations of His universal and detailed intellections; quiddities are these intellections, understood as proceeding one from another—not in the sense that new intellections arise in the Real (exalted is He above anything unworthy of Him), but in the sense that some are understood as posterior to others in rank. All are everlasting intellections, constant in their manner; in knowledge they are intelligible, and knowledge relates to them according to the demands of their realities.

pairs.ar: ومقتضى حقائقها على نحوين: أحدهما: تعقلها من حيث استهلاك كثرتها في وحدة الحق، وهو تعقل المفصل في المجمل، كمشاهدة العالم العاقل بعين العلم في النواة الواحدة ما فيها بالقوة من الأغصان والأوراق والثمر، والذي في كل فرد من أفراد ذلك الثمر مثل ما في النواة الأولى، وهكذا إلى غير النهاية. والنحو الآخر: تعقّل أحكام الوحدة جملة بعد جملة، فيتعقل كل جملة بما تشتمل عليه من الماهيات التي هي صورة تلك التعقّلات المتكثرة المعددة للوجود الواحد، وهكذا عكس الاستهلاك الأول المشار إليه؛ فإن ذلك عبارة عن استهلاك الكثرة في الوحدة، وهذا هو استهلاك الوحدة في الكثرة فليعلم ذلك.
pairs.en: The demands of their realities may be considered in two ways. First, they are apprehended insofar as their multiplicity is absorbed in the Real's unity: the detailed within the undifferentiated, as when a knowing observer sees in a single seed, through knowledge, the branches, leaves, and fruit potentially contained within it—and in every individual fruit a counterpart of what the original seed contained, without end. The second way is to apprehend the determinations of unity, group after group, each group with the quiddities comprised in it, which are the forms of those manifold intellections by which the one existence is considered in multiplicity. This is the reverse of the former absorption: there multiplicity was absorbed in unity; here unity is absorbed in multiplicity. Understand this.
